expected.note: req.body.passphrase/reminder concatenated into raw INSERT run via sequelize.query.
req.params.username concatenated into raw SELECT on an unauthenticated route; dumps all passphrases.
req.body.search interpolated into a MongoDB $where JS expression; breaks out of the public-only filter.
req.params.command passed to child_process.exec; any authenticated user gets OS command execution.
Unauthenticated :release param concatenated into XPath over config.xml, which holds DB credentials.
Unauthenticated SOAP body parsed by libxmljs2 with noent/dtdload; external entities are resolved and reflected in the response.
Notes XML import parses with noent/dtdload/huge; entity expansion allows file reads into notes and billion-laughs DoS.
Parsed username is interpolated unescaped into the SOAP response XML, so extra elements (e.g. role) can be spoofed.
Body username/bio are interpolated unescaped into the XML response (application/xml), so elements or markup can be injected.
User input concatenated into an LDAP filter; the simulated backend returns all users and an admin password for injected filters.
Raw username (and spoofable X-Forwarded-For) written to the login log without stripping newlines, so log entries can be forged.
Stored username reflected in a 409 text/plain response with no nosniff header; XSS only in MIME-sniffing browsers.
Base64 body data passed to node-serialize unserialize, which evaluates embedded function expressions (RCE).
Unauthenticated XML-RPC dvws.CheckUptime fetches any user-supplied URL with needle.get (blind SSRF to internal and metadata hosts).
req.body.filename is joined and path.resolve'd without containment, then res.download serves any readable file.
updateUserUploadFile writes attacker-controlled content to an attacker-controlled filePath with no normalization, so files can be written anywhere.
Uploaded file name (only checked for an .xml suffix) is concatenated into the destination path under the public web root; traversal sequences in the name escape the user directory.
Recursive merge of user JSON metadata (called at line 42) does not block __proto__/constructor keys, polluting Object.prototype process-wide.
Unauthenticated registration passes req.body directly to new User(), so admin=true can be set at signup.
Unauthenticated XML profile import updates any username taken from the XML and accepts an admin flag, granting admin to any account.
Notes fetched by sequential numeric id with no ownership check, exposing other users' private notes.
Any user updates any note by name with raw req.body (no owner filter), including reassigning the user field.
Any authenticated user can delete any note by name; no ownership check.
GET /v2/passphrase/:username has no auth or ownership check, so anyone can read any user's passphrases.
GET /v2/users needs only a valid token (no admin check) and returns every user document including bcrypt hashes and admin flags.
Admin-only sysinfo endpoint is guarded only by validateToken, so any user can reach it (compounds the command injection).
/v2/admin/logs returns all login attempt logs (usernames, IPs) to any authenticated user.
express-jwt-permissions guard.check is placed after controllers that already respond, and reads req.identity which is never set, so permission checks never run.
Unauthenticated userFindbyId returns any User including the password hash field exposed in the schema.
Unauthenticated userSearchByUsername confirms usernames and returns _id and admin flag (feeds userFindbyId).
Unauthenticated noteFindbyId returns any note by sequential id, including private notes.
readNote checks only that a token exists, then returns any user's notes by name with no ownership filter.
Unauthenticated getPassphrase returns stored passphrases to anyone who guesses a reminder value.
JWT HS256 secret is the dictionary word 'access', committed in .env; tokens can be cracked offline and forged with admin permissions.
Admin user-creation accepts a cookie-based token and parses JSON from text/plain bodies, so a cross-site simple request can create admin accounts.
Login returns 404 'User X not found' versus 401 for a wrong password, which enumerates valid usernames.
Login rate-limit key comes from the client-controlled X-Forwarded-For header, so rotating it bypasses the limit.
Export endpoint checks a password for any username in the body with no rate limit, acting as an unthrottled password oracle.
allowBatchedHttpRequests lets many guesses (getPassphrase/userLogin) run in one HTTP request, evading per-request throttling.
Unauthenticated /api/v1/info returns process.env (JWT secret, DB creds) and runtime config; only the /v2 path is blocked.
userLogin returns the stored bcrypt hash for any existing username before (and regardless of) password verification.
Successful REST login returns the full user document, including the bcrypt hash, in the response body.
Registration response echoes the stored bcrypt password hash.
GraphQL introspection and playground are enabled in the running server, exposing the full schema including the password field and file-write mutation.
CORS reflects any Origin with credentials true, so attacker sites can read authenticated responses (cookie-auth endpoints).
Logout redirects to 'http://' + an unvalidated path parameter (open redirect).
Uploads are stored under the express.static public/ root and validated only by an .xml suffix, so attacker-controlled content is served from the app origin.

must_not_report.reason: The reminder is escaped with sequelize.escape before concatenation, so this string-built SQL is not injectable (the issue there is missing auth, labelled separately).
The $where string is built only from the constant 'public'; there is no user input.
Lists notes filtered by the token's user; correctly scoped.
Only whitelisted fields are copied and the owner comes from the verified token; no mass assignment.
Requires a token and sets the owner from context.user; fields are explicitly listed.
Admin status is re-checked against the DB and the new user is built from explicit fields; the authz check itself is sound (CSRF is labelled separately).
Profile is looked up by the verified token's user and returns only username/bio/admin; no IDOR or hash leak.
Directory listing is scoped to the token's own username directory; no user-supplied path.
Loads a fixed bundled fixture at startup with xmldom; no user input reaches the parser.
xml2js (sax-based) does not resolve external entities, so this parse is not an XXE sink (the authz flaw is labelled separately).
xmlrpc's sax-based Deserializer does not expand DTD entities; not an XXE sink.
Passwords are hashed with bcrypt at cost 10 before save; this is not weak crypto.

debatable.note: ignoreExpiration true makes tokens valid forever; increases the impact of stolen tokens but is not a standalone exploit.
Apollo debug true includes stack traces in GraphQL errors.
Raw DB/library errors returned to clients in many handlers (also notes.js, users.js, soap err.toString()); aids exploitation.
Handlers split req.headers.authorization without a null check (getProfile, checkadmin, notes) and throw; mostly 500s, not a crash.
MySQL root credentials committed in .env and fixtures/xml/config.xml; deployment default, exposed further via /v1/info and XPath.
Public OpenAPI spec and Swagger UI list hidden admin endpoints; discovery aid, not a vuln on its own.
auth_token cookie lacks Secure and SameSite; also set even on failed login (value 'undefined').
Docs call this enumeration, but unknown users also return role 'user', so only admin accounts are distinguishable.
Per-key map grows without eviction; with spoofed X-Forwarded-For keys memory grows unbounded.
system.listMethods exposes callable methods; docs list it as XML-RPC enumeration.

algorithms list allows "none"; the library rejects it when a secret is set (algorithms includes 'none', but jsonwebtoken 9.0.3 rejects unsigned tokens whenever a secret is supplied ('jwt signature is required'), and JWT_SECRET is always set. Same applies to the duplicated options in server.js, users.js, notes.js, files.js, passphrase.js.)
